category: Metadata/context platform sold as the context layer for AI
licence_pricing: Proprietary; no public list price (pricing page redirects to sales contact; enterprise quote; price unknown)
deployment: SaaS with single-tenant options; deploy anywhere to Cortex, Genie, Claude, Codex via MCP server
inputs: Connectors across data and business systems (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, BI tools, Slack, Teams and more); lineage; business glossary and decision history
entry_criteria: Enterprise catalog adoption; connectors configured; context repos curated; agents onboarded through MCP
how_layer_built: Connectors build an enterprise graph; AI Context Agents draft ontology, descriptions, metrics, quality rules, glossary and READMEs; Context Engineering Studio bootstraps repos, runs eval suites, deploys to agents and observes traces and drift
automation_level: Medium-high: AI drafts context and evals gate it, but humans commit every definition
human_in_loop: AI plus human: versioned context repos labelled AI + human, git-style log, eval suites, approval on deploy
artifacts_exit_criteria: Versioned context repos, evaluation suites, prompts/definitions, MCP server, agent traces and drift reports
time_versioning: Context repo versioning (for example v3.1.2) and drift monitoring; no bitemporal fact semantics documented
lineage_provenance: Lineage and provenance are core products (Enterprise Data Graph, column lineage, decision history)
agent_consumption: MCP server delivers governed definitions, lineage and policies to Claude, ChatGPT and custom agents; context reads, not sized answer packs
problems_solved: Governed definitions and lineage for agents; stops agents inventing business meaning; one context source across models
documented_outcomes: Vendor self-reported: 400+ enterprises, 8B context reads in 90 days, 87% of customers say generated context is on par or better than human-written; not measured
limits: Catalog-scale prerequisite; human curation load; opaque pricing; context is metadata not an answer; no documented budget or per-line evidence grade
gap_for_us: Runtime packing with hard budget, per-line grade and an explicit dropped-facts record; usable without a catalog
notes: Outcome numbers are marketing claims (grade C if relied on); pricing page redirected to contact form

category: Graph context layer plus graph-native agent memory
licence_pricing: Proprietary; no public price (launched 2026-10-20, design partners being taken; pricing unknown)
deployment: Neo4j graph platform (Aura or self-managed) with Context Studio control plane; headless CLI and Python packages
inputs: Existing data sources such as Databricks and Snowflake; enterprise architecture and process knowledge
entry_criteria: Enterprise ontology modelling effort; design-partner engagement during launch window
how_layer_built: Predefined 6-layer business ontology (Neo4j says built from patterns across hundreds of deployments); Context Build and Runtime builds the ontology and exposes it; Context Studio is the control plane with visual builder and MCP server setup; GraphRAG retrievers query it
automation_level: Medium: some build automation from sources, but ontology layers are vendor-pattern-driven and human-mapped
human_in_loop: Visual ontology builder, change management, governance in Context Studio; no outcome measurement published
artifacts_exit_criteria: Ontology graph, Context Memory (short, long and reasoning memory with skill distillation), MCP servers, agent setup artifacts
time_versioning: Built-in change management; Context Memory records reasoning paths and events over time; no pubished bitemporal fact-answer semantics
lineage_provenance: Relationships and their provenance are first-class; logs agent reasoning and operational paths as a permanent record
agent_consumption: Agents consume graph traversal results, memory and MCP tools from an orchestration layer
problems_solved: Shared knowledge layer so agents know what customer, account, supplier and risk mean; persistent memory; process-guided agents
documented_outcomes: None measured; launch covered by trade press with vendor quotes
limits: New product (9 days old at access date); requires graph ontology build; no public price, accuracy or case-study evidence
gap_for_us: Auto-build a lightweight ontology from raw schema without the 6-layer modelling exercise; carry evidence grades into answers
notes: Product page returned partial HTML; launch details from trade press (grade C) and vendor press release

category: Enterprise AI platform on a modelled Ontology
licence_pricing: Proprietary; no public list price (platform subscription via Foundry enrollment; price unknown)
deployment: Foundry enrollment: cloud, on-premises and government environments
inputs: Enterprise data sources integrated into Foundry; Ontology object types, links and actions
entry_criteria: Foundry enrollment plus an Ontology; security markings and governance configured
how_layer_built: Ontology modelled by hand (object types, links, actions); agents built with AIP Logic, AIP Chatbot Studio (formerly Agent Studio) and Agent SDK; AIP Evals for testing
automation_level: Medium: rich tooling and evals, but the semantic model of the business is human-modelled
human_in_loop: Staged writes give an explicit human approval step before Ontology changes; audit trails and markings
artifacts_exit_criteria: Ontology-backed agents, functions, evals, session logs, audit trails
time_versioning: Historical lineage in governance tooling; time semantics for Ontology edits via evals, not bitemporal answer packing
lineage_provenance: Built-in governance, audit, security markings and historical lineage
agent_consumption: Agent receives Ontology objects/links/functions as tools plus retrieval context types with citations
problems_solved: Typed enterprise context for agents; approval before action; secure access to sensitive data
documented_outcomes: Vendor documentation and case studies; no independent measured outcome in this pass
limits: Heavy platform and services dependency; opaque pricing; manual ontology; context layer inseparable from the platform
gap_for_us: Cheap, local, source-first context with per-fact provenance and explicit budget; no platform lock-in
notes: Staged writes and citations are documented; core differentiator is the action-level approval gate

licence_pricing: MIT licence (code free); pay LLM tokens for indexing and query; indexing documented as expensive
deployment: Local Python pipeline (CLI and library); any configured LLM provider
inputs: Unstructured text corpora (TextUnits); structured tabular connectors not the focus
entry_criteria: Python environment plus an LLM endpoint plus a corpus; prompt tuning strongly recommended before production use
how_layer_built: LLM extracts entities, relationships and claims from TextUnits; Leiden clustering builds a community hierarchy; community summaries generated bottom-up; query modes Global, Local, DRIFT and Basic
automation_level: High automation for extraction and summarisation; human work is prompt tuning
human_in_loop: None built in; prompt tuning is manual and recommended; no approval workflow
artifacts_exit_criteria: Knowledge graph parquet outputs, community reports, LanceDB vectors, query-engine context
time_versioning: Breaking-changes document and migration notebooks; re-indexing needed on major versions; no temporal semantics
lineage_provenance: TextUnit references give coarse source traceability; no per-fact confidence grade
agent_consumption: Agent receives passages and community summaries injected into its prompt by the calling application
problems_solved: Holistic questions over private narrative data; connect-the-dots synthesis that baseline RAG misses
documented_outcomes: Microsoft Research reports quality improvement over baseline RAG; no independent measurement in this pass
limits: README states project is largely in maintenance mode and will not accept new PRs; expensive indexing; no permissions, approval, budget or enterprise connectors
gap_for_us: Structured sources plus provenance-graded, budgeted packs with human-reviewable definitions
notes: README warning about maintenance mode is important competitive evidence

category: Open integration protocol for LLM context and tools (not a layer)
licence_pricing: Open specification; no licence fee; governed as a Series of LF Projects (Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation)
deployment: Any host and server; local stdio or HTTP transports
inputs: Servers expose resources, prompts and tools; hosts supply models and user consent
entry_criteria: A host (agent/IDE) plus MCP servers; OAuth and consent flows for protected servers
how_layer_built: Servers expose resources/prompts/tools; clients may offer sampling, roots and elicitation; the host decides what enters the context window
automation_level: High for integration; the protocol does not automate what is true, relevant or permitted
human_in_loop: Protocol mandates user consent and explicit tool authorisation; no content review or approval object
artifacts_exit_criteria: Tool definitions, tool results, resources; host-side prompts and sampling
time_versioning: Protocol versioning (2025-06-18 read here; 2026-07-28 published); no content versioning
lineage_provenance: No provenance semantics; tool descriptions are explicitly treated as untrusted in the spec
agent_consumption: Agent receives tool definitions and results under host-controlled context budget
problems_solved: Standard integration of tools and data into agents; avoids one bespoke connector per tool
documented_outcomes: Vendor blog claims about half a billion monthly SDK downloads; not independently measured
limits: Not a context layer: no ontology, ranking, permission model for content, budget accounting or provenance; security depends on implementers
gap_for_us: Become the MCP endpoint that servers and hosts call; ship a bounded, graded pack as an MCP resource/tool
notes: Specification quotes consent principles; governance from site footer (LF Projects)

category: Enterprise search, assistant and agents over an Enterprise Graph
licence_pricing: Proprietary; per-user per-month seat licence, amount not published; LLM usage billed at model rates via Glean Model Hub (table dated 2026-10-20); unknown total cost
deployment: Glean-hosted single-tenant with regional data residency
inputs: 250+ connectors; documents, people, messages, tickets and business apps; permission metadata
entry_criteria: Seat licences plus connectors plus SSO/RBAC configuration
how_layer_built: Automated indexing builds a knowledge graph and hybrid search index with custom semantic and lexical models; permissions enforced at retrieval; saved and learned memory; agents built in-product
automation_level: High: indexing, relevance and permissions automated; agent behaviour configured by admins
human_in_loop: Admin configuration and agent governance; RBAC; no per-fact human review
artifacts_exit_criteria: Search, Chat and Agents APIs; remote MCP server; agent library; insights dashboards
time_versioning: Continuous indexing and freshness management; memory over time; no bitemporal answer semantics documented
lineage_provenance: Permission enforcement (Glean Protect), citations, audit logs; no per-fact confidence grade
agent_consumption: Agent receives permission-filtered documents and people context with citations, via APIs or MCP tools
problems_solved: Enterprise search plus assistant/agents over company knowledge; permission-safe answers; one assistant across apps
documented_outcomes: Vendor claims and customer logos; no independent measured outcome in this pass
limits: SaaS-only; per-seat cost; context is documents and people, not structured metrics; no answer budget or evidence grades; connector coverage is the product
gap_for_us: Fuse structured facts and documents into one graded, budgeted pack; run locally without connectors
notes: Usage model and Model Hub rates from docs; seat price itself not published

category: Temporal context graph and agent memory service
licence_pricing: Graphiti engine Apache-2.0; Zep Cloud 2026-10-29 list: Flex $125/mo (50,000 credits, then $25/10,000; 5 Context MCP seats); Flex Plus $375/mo (200,000 credits, then $75/40,000; 15 seats); Enterprise custom; free prototyping at 10,000 credits/mo
deployment: Zep Cloud managed; Cloud with customer keys (BYOK); Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC) on Enterprise
inputs: Conversations, documents and business data ingested as episodes; custom entity and edge types
entry_criteria: Zep account and API key; MCP server seats by plan; entity/edge customisation on paid plans
how_layer_built: Temporal context graph: episodes are processed into entities, edges and communities with validity intervals; retrieval over graph plus embeddings; custom extraction instructions on Flex Plus
automation_level: High for extraction and graph maintenance; humans set schema and instructions
human_in_loop: Custom extraction instructions and entity/edge types are human-configured; no content approval workflow outside Enterprise audit
artifacts_exit_criteria: Context graph, memory retrieval API, Context MCP Server, observations and webhooks
time_versioning: Temporal edges and validity intervals (core design); audit logs on Enterprise; API logs 1 to 7 days by plan
lineage_provenance: Temporal graph gives provenance of when facts were true; no per-line confidence grade documented
agent_consumption: Agent receives retrieved memories and entity context over API or Context MCP Server
problems_solved: Agent memory and user/account context over time; contradictions reduced by temporal modelling
documented_outcomes: S&P Global Market Intelligence quote on vendor page calls it a temporal context graph (April 2026); no independent measured outcome
limits: Credit-based pricing depends on episode size; memory service not an enterprise metric governance layer; no answer budget
gap_for_us: Combine memory with governed metrics and definitions; one pack instead of two retrieval calls
notes: Pricing page is explicit about credits and MCP seats

category: Stateful agent harness with self-managed memory
licence_pricing: Apache-2.0 for letta-code (brand assets excluded from licence); Letta Cloud commercial, price unknown; local backend optional
deployment: Local CLI, self-hosted server, managed sandbox, Letta Cloud (default)
inputs: Agent conversations, memory blocks, skills; user-configured model API keys
entry_criteria: Install CLI; sign in to Letta Cloud or run a local backend; MCP and model configuration
how_layer_built: Agents rewrite their own memory blocks, skills and system prompt; context tracked in git via MemFS; subagents, hooks, permissions, schedules and channels
automation_level: High for self-managed memory and learning; no enterprise source ingestion
human_in_loop: Human sets permission modes and hooks; the agent edits its own context
artifacts_exit_criteria: Agent memory blocks, MemFS git history, skills, conversation transcripts
time_versioning: MemFS gives git versioning of agent context over time
lineage_provenance: Agent-level memory provenance only; no enterprise lineage or per-fact confidence grade
agent_consumption: Agent receives its rewritten memory blocks and system prompt in its own window
problems_solved: Long-horizon stateful agents with persistent memory; self-improving behaviour across sessions
documented_outcomes: Vendor research and docs; no independent measured outcome in this pass
limits: Per-agent memory, not a shared enterprise context layer; no connectors, permissions model for enterprise data, or governance
gap_for_us: A per-agent context pack that is shared, graded, permission-aware and reproducible across agents
notes: Letta moved from MemGPT-era server to Letta Code; old API server archived

category: Storage layer for embeddings, not a context layer
licence_pricing: Pinecone 2026-10-29 list: Free; Builder $20/mo flat; Standard $50/mo minimum usage then pay-as-you-go; Enterprise custom. Weaviate and Qdrant open source and self-hostable (licences not re-verified this pass)
deployment: Managed cloud (Pinecone) or self-hosted open source
inputs: Chunks/embeddings plus metadata; document pipelines supply the text
entry_criteria: An embedding model, an index and a caller that builds queries; no governance prerequisite
how_layer_built: Embed chunks, index vectors (dense, sparse, full text), similarity search at query time
automation_level: High for indexing and search; zero automation of meaning, relevance policy or packing
human_in_loop: None; the caller owns chunking, quality and permissions
artifacts_exit_criteria: Index plus top-k retrieval; no artifact that describes meaning or evidence
time_versioning: Index versions or namespaces; no temporal fact semantics
lineage_provenance: Metadata filters only; caller must enforce permissions; no lineage or provenance
agent_consumption: Agent receives top-k chunks and metadata; context budget and packing left to the caller
problems_solved: Fast semantic storage and retrieval at scale
documented_outcomes: Vendor benchmarks and customer stories; not measured in this pass
limits: Not a layer: no ontology, definitions, permissions enforcement, approval, budget accounting or provenance
gap_for_us: Use as storage under our packer; compete on the layer above, not on the index
notes: Explicitly labelled storage, not a context layer; the not-a-layer judgement is our inference
